channel.title: How
channel.description: Here’s how I build. Notes from a decade of front-end work — Angular, architecture, and the tools around them — written down as I go.

item.title: MCP belongs in front of the APIs you already have
item.description: How to add MCP in an API repo so agents can query latest email-threat detections and search without scraping a UI.

item.title: Remotes still need a route
item.description: How an independently deployed Angular remote dies in the host when routing and auth contracts are implied instead of written down.

item.title: Affected is the CI
item.description: How Nx affected keeps a multi-product Angular monorepo honest in CI — and what happens when the graph lies.

item.title: Teachers and donors are not the same user
item.description: How a Node API for a child-education NGO splits teacher and donor access so progress can be shared without leaking learners.

item.title: Go after years of Node
item.description: What actually changes when someone who ships Node and Java starts writing small Go tools.

item.title: Share the tokens, not the components
item.description: How a design-token library keeps Angular micro frontends looking like one product without a fat shared component dump.

item.title: The email template is a contract
item.description: How to version an HTML email template so placeholders, loops, escaping, and i18n stay a stable contract with the sending service.

item.title: Tags are the build graph
item.description: How Nx module-boundary tags keep Angular libraries and micro frontends from depending on the wrong things.

item.title: Photos of children are not “just uploads”
item.description: How a small Node API for a child-education NGO stores photos with consent, private objects, and signed URLs.

item.title: Small Go CLIs still earn their keep
item.description: How a tiny Go command stays honest — flags, exit codes, and tests you can run in one file.

item.title: A shell is not a folder
item.description: How to split an Angular micro frontend so the shell stays a host, not a junk drawer of remotes.

item.title: HTML email is still tables
item.description: How to build a complex HTML email as a front-end artifact — nested tables, inline CSS, and a preview that is not Gmail.

item.title: One repo when you ship several products
item.description: How an Nx monorepo earns its keep when several Angular products share libraries, tooling, and a release cadence.

item.title: The HTML the crawler actually gets
item.description: How to check prerendered Angular HTML for real content, social cards, JSON-LD, and a 404 that stays a 404.

item.title: Metadata belongs in the resolver, not ngOnInit
item.description: How to set title, canonical, and Open Graph tags in a route resolver so prerendered HTML already has them.

item.title: Angular 22 prerender without the ceremony
item.description: How to ship crawlable Angular pages with outputMode static, a resolver for metadata, and no CMS.

item.title: Zoneless means you meant the update
item.description: How to run Angular without Zone.js so only signal writes and explicit marks update the view.

item.title: inject() is the constructor now
item.description: A standalone component can take what it needs with inject. Local UI state belongs in a signal.

item.title: Inputs that are already signals
item.description: How input, output, and model replace decorator inputs when a shared card has to react to the parent.

item.title: The filter is a signal, not a field you remember to update
item.description: How a writable signal and a computed list replace a field plus a manual refresh on a filter chip.

item.title: Stop putting *ngIf on a live list
item.description: How @if, @for, and @empty replace *ngIf and *ngFor on a list that actually changes.

item.title: Migrate in this order or you will migrate twice
item.description: How to sequence an Angular migration on a federated product so each step can ship without undoing the last one.

item.title: The version bump is not the migration
item.description: Bumping Angular on an Enate-era product does not give you the Mimecast-era app shape — you still have to change how the app is built.
